title: Decimal digit count of a fixed 565248-bit object

located_defect.lean_text:
abbrev PublishedDecimalConversionAt (H : Nat) : Prop :=
  FitsBits bits H -> HasDecDigits H 390000
def UniversalPublishedDecimalConversion : Prop := ∀ H : Nat, PublishedDecimalConversionAt H
located_defect.description: Stored post line 0028 fixes the object's size at 69 x 8 x 1024 = 565248 bits; line 0030 converts this bit count into a decimal digit count ("multiply by log_10 (2) +~ .69") and states about 390,000 decimal digits. Read as a statement about every value fitting the 565248-bit budget (PublishedDecimalConversionAt, UniversalPublishedDecimalConversion, with the stored digit convention HasDecDigits) this is the located defect. Supply the correct decimal digit count for the budget and prove (i) every fitting value has at most that many digits and (ii) the largest fitting value has exactly that many (so the count is the least one); then state the same count in Mathlib's Nat.digits. Nothing about the digits of pi is part of this record.
